311. Ansible rebuild path not demonstrated because setup was done manually first
Batch: 7778 | Execution: 2026-09-28__22-57-18 | Severity: Medium
Task: file-integrity-baseline-ansible-ubuntu24-7778
Problem: AIDE was installed directly outside Ansible and its baseline database existed before the playbook ran. The initialization task therefore skipped work. The playbook managed the resulting state, but that successful rerun did not prove it could create the baseline from a fresh host.
Why a production administrator should care: A successful rerun after manual repair can hide an unreproducible deployment. Verify the actual provisioning path from a controlled baseline and recovery without manual intervention.

328. DHCP Ansible rerun followed direct CLI provisioning on the router
Batch: 7778 | Execution: 2026-09-28__23-27-33 | Severity: Medium
Task: dhcp-server-ansible-rhel10-7778
Problem: Several vyos_config attempts failed, and manual CLI sessions established and saved the working interface/DHCP configuration. A revised playbook then reported no router changes. This validates convergence on existing state rather than actual clean-baseline provisioning by the retained automation.
Why a production administrator should care: A positive request, manual run, or no-change rerun may exercise a different path than unattended deployment or unauthorized-client denial. Missing evidence is not a proven breach.

findings.title: Ansible no-change rerun followed manual DHCP provisioning
findings.classification_basis: Two Ansible deployment attempts failed, and working router syntax was applied by direct CLI sessions. The corrected playbook then reported no changes against that manually configured state. This proves convergence on existing state, not that the playbook can create the required configuration from scratch.

330. Ansible no-change rerun followed manual DHCP provisioning
Batch: 7778 | Execution: 2026-09-28__23-27-33 | Severity: Medium
Task: dhcp-server-ansible-rhel9-7778
